title: India re-elected to UN telecom body's council with 151 votes, ahead of China
dek: India came third among 15 candidates for 13 Asia-Pacific seats on the International Telecommunication Union's governing council at the conference in Doha.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the UN agency that coordinates radio spectrum, satellite orbits and telecom standards, for the 2027-2030 term, the ITU's official results from its Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha show.

India won 151 votes in Region E (Asia and Australasia), where 15 countries stood for 13 seats. It came third, behind Qatar (165) and Saudi Arabia (155), and ahead of Japan and the United Arab Emirates (149 each), Indonesia (148), Kuwait (147), Malaysia (145), Australia and South Korea (144 each), China and Thailand (139 each) and Bahrain (125). Pakistan (115) and Iraq (106) were not elected.

The 48-member Council runs the ITU between its four-yearly plenipotentiary conferences, overseeing its policies, strategic and financial plans and working groups. Its decisions feed into the rules on spectrum and satellite slots that shape India's 5G and 6G plans and its satellite internet sector. Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia called it a "resounding victory" that reflected global trust in India's capabilities, and said India's resolution proposals at the conference had received broad support.

Earlier in the conference, on 12 November, Doreen Bogdan-Martin of the United States was re-elected ITU Secretary-General with 164 votes, the ITU said.
